authority: worker-level measurement only; no gate verdict, no node transition, no canonical write, no validation_status promotion
question: Is the load-bearing generated acceptance fixture directory artifacts/formulation/evidence/rebased_fixtures/ bound by any pin, and what can a pin-blind actor do to the acceptance evidence at fixed pinned inputs?
method: Read-only + sandbox-only. (1) enumerate the exact file set run_acceptance.py reads; (2) measure per-file sha256 and the listing digest; (3) cross-check against artifacts/formulation/FROZEN.json files{} and against the transitive bindings recorded in the pinned corpus record; (4) build a fail-closed binding checker; (5) run the pinned stage tools over sandbox copies of the corpus in pristine/deleted/modified/extra variants and compute the exact run_acceptance.py corpus verdict logic; (6) re-measure every input at T1 and report drift.

preregistered_predictions.statement: FROZEN rev29 files{} covers 0 of the 33 files under artifacts/formulation/evidence/rebased_fixtures/.
preregistered_predictions.kill: >0 covered => scope of the finding narrows to the uncovered remainder

preregistered_predictions.statement: run_acceptance.py reads the corpus by glob("*.yaml"): 31 mutant rows + 2 control rows at the measured file set.
preregistered_predictions.kill: different enumeration (e.g. fixed list) => the exposure mechanism is different

preregistered_predictions.statement: Pristine sandbox corpus: union catch 31/31, controls 2/2, corpus-level verdict PASS (match the generation-time numbers in the pinned corpus record).
preregistered_predictions.kill: any pristine escape => the pinned record is not reproducible on the on-disk bytes

preregistered_predictions.statement: Deleting one mutant file yields union catch 30/30 and corpus-level verdict PASS: a silent, pin-blind weakening of the acceptance corpus.
preregistered_predictions.kill: deletion is detected by a pin/checker at fixed pinned inputs => the exposure is closed

preregistered_predictions.statement: Replacing one mutant with a copy of the canonical base yields >=1 union escape and corpus-level verdict FAIL: tamper is detected only if the pipeline is re-run.
preregistered_predictions.kill: no escape => the mutation is inert

preregistered_predictions.statement: Adding one extra benign yaml yields 1 union escape and corpus-level verdict FAIL (count inflation, loud not silent).
preregistered_predictions.kill: extra file is ignored => the glob does not read it

preregistered_predictions.statement: check_fixture_binding.py accepts the pristine manifest and detects missing, extra and byte-modified files (fail-closed).
The on-disk corpus is stale-bound: its recorded base_sha256 (1bb78ce9) differs from the live canonical C0 at T0; regeneration at the live C0 in a sandbox is byte-deterministic.
preregistered_predictions.kill: regeneration is non-deterministic or the recorded base matches live

preregistered_predictions.statement: No canonical input hash changes between T0 and T1 during this lifecycle.
preregistered_predictions.kill: any measured input drift is reported as drift, not hidden

exposure_statement: A pin over the corpus record (semantic_escape_rebased.json 7e44de0e) binds the recorded fixture NAMES and the generation-time verdicts, but not the fixture BYTES. Because run_acceptance.py re-reads the directory by glob at run time, at fixed pinned inputs a deletion of one mutant weakens the effective corpus while the corpus-level verdict remains PASS.
falsifier: The finding is void if the next authorized freeze covers every file under artifacts/formulation/evidence/rebased_fixtures/ (or the pipeline verifies fixture bytes against a pin before use), and the FROZEN-declared corpus record reproduces those bytes. The P4 exposure is void if a pinned checker rejects the deletion at fixed pinned inputs.
stop_rule: If a canonical file must change to complete the measurement, STOP and report the item as out of scope. All tool runs happen on sandbox copies.
